_doc: Generator knobs. Every knob is a [easy, hard] pair interpolated by the search's pressure p in [0, 1], then jittered by the mutation step. Only burn, length, swarm and waves are real difficulty levers (outpost-ops#85): fuel0 0.75, startCurrency 0, costScale 1 and margin 0.37 are constants, machines is the automate goal's converters-running count (2 up to the level's converters), the noise settings sit at the middle of their old range (constants too), and the map-dressing knobs listed under dressing are drawn from the level seed. Costs are in currency at costScale 1 unless keyed salvage.*.

familyKnobs._doc: Composer knob search (ops docs/reference/addons.md): per-family [p=0, p=1] ends that replace the knobs entry for that family's levels. Cost scale and fuel burn move with the pressure so the search can tune the composed add-on set; rescue's pod freeze clock, pod count and crate count too (the counts follow the search pressure, which starts from the slot's target).

rings._doc: Half extents of the perimeter ring around the core (world units), and sections per side (top/bottom, left/right).
rings._podRoom: outpost-ops#202: depth of open ground kept beyond a gate rockfall band for the pods (the wavefront layout moves north or west as one piece to make it).

ranger._doc: Ranger hire pad inside the hunting grounds, clear of the burrow models: render-3d ART_M and the zone.prey.l1/l2 half sizes from meshy.built.json (art metres), plus a gap (world units).

traderRoute._doc: Grid cell, clearance from footprints and walls, and half the gate door opening (world units).

lots._doc: Lots and streets (POLISH-PLAN item 7B): streets of street units cross at the core (its plaza) and repeat every block + street; square lots of block units between them; buildings keep to one lot along each axis they fit.

defendWaves._doc: Swarmlings per wave = swarm knob x share: wave 0 firstShare, then +earlyGrowth per wave; weak raids each come from one attack side; from wave lateFrom on (levels with towers or guards to buy) +lateGrowth per wave, packed at lateGap seconds apart instead of gap, from every attack side. Raiders = swarm x (late)Raiders x wave index. The early raids grow until they drop dropsPerEarlyNeed x the walls and one tower per attack side; then the packed waves grow together until all but the last drop dropsPerNeed x the core of the purchase ladder (walls, the first guards, med bay, and a tower on every socket standing from the start, at their rising prices: Batch 3 sizes the waves against it; tower levels, more guards and later sockets are left to build to the end); each packed wave stays lateStep x the wave before it. R5 (Doug: growth first, price cuts only for the rest): a wave's attackers arrive one at a time and the good bot has 120 s after the last wave starts, so no wave spawns for longer than spawnMax s (its gap tightens, down to minGap). The packed waves grow (at most fullGrowMax more times, and only while the biggest still fits spawnMax at minGap) until all but the last drop the whole purchase list (every scrap pad once, tower levels and later sockets included, the guards a train-N goal needs, at the prices defence growth raises them to, cheapest first); where that is not enough the level's defence price growth eases by growthStep toward 1, then its scrap prices scale down until the drops pay for the list. With towers or guards to buy there are at least lateFrom + 2 waves. On med bay levels a probe raid (raid) comes through a breach in a quiet side at t s, before the player has scrap to wall it. A defend survive goal lasts surviveTail s past the start of the wave before the last. Denser, not bigger (Doug: the last waves dragged on): once sized, every wave from the first one over waveCap points (HP) on is split into even pieces of at most waveCap, arriving lateWaveGap x waveGap s apart, closer (down to lateWaveMin s) where needed so the last piece starts no later than the old last wave did; the warlords are placed again by the count rule and their points come out of the swarmlings, so the total points and drops stay the same. waveCap 0 is off.
defendWaves.mix_doc: Mixed waves (outpost-ops#92): from the second wave on, a share of each wave's swarmling points comes as creatures (mid: the early raids; late: the packed waves), 1 creature for 3 swarmlings so points and drops stay the same; a late wave always holds swarmlings, raiders and creatures. Then each late wave gains late.extra x its points as more creatures, as far as it still spawns within spawnMax and stays within waveCap points.
defendWaves.warlords_doc: Several warlords (outpost-ops#92 part 2): on levels with the bosses feature the final wave carries the warlord count of the last row whose difficulty target the level reaches ([target, warlords]; below the first row, or with no target, 1). Extra warlords add their points and drops to the wave, so the wave sizing counts them; when the waves are split by waveCap the last piece carries them all.

storms._doc: Dust storms (dust_storms feature): warned warn s ahead, lasting duration s. R5 #29: a run where the player stops helping at a storm's start (the hauler and other hires carry on) must lose before that storm ends; until it does, the storm lasts growStep s longer, up to maxDuration, and a level still survivable then is rejected.

site._doc: 88.2 (outpost-ops#88): clearing the slide frees the site of a later building. Joins the draw only on levels that raise this building (one with no crew pads around it, so it can move); the slide is rect [w, h], the building stands at `at` and its pad at `pad`, both offsets from the rect's top-left. The rect stays the usual slide size: a bigger one closes the traders' way to the kiosk line on Level 105; only the roof rises past the rubble.

hunting._doc: 88.4 (outpost-ops#88, Doug 2026-11-18): on a new level whose hunting grounds have a ranger (the catch is sold), a rock slide hides the grounds with this seeded chance. The rubble lies against the side of the hopper flats nearest the Core, `depth` deep and `overhang` wider than the flats on each side, and the ranger's hire pad needs the slide cleared. Existing levels keep their layout (no pack regeneration).
hunting._doc88_3: 88.3: the other three sides of the flats are closed with `ridge` terrain `wall` deep (corners included), so the cleared slide is the only way in; `wall` is past the player's melee reach (player.attackRange 40; the block margin only applies along y).

beatBreakers._doc: Play-shape beat-breakers (outpost-ops#151, 151.4; Doug: no phase over 40% of the level). On these families, with workers and a cashier, a ladder of dearer hires stands between the farm worker and the cashier (farm worker -> lateHires in order -> cashier), so the bot buys one about every fifth of the level instead of all three hires in the first third and then running one collect-and-sell loop to the end. Each purchase is a play-shape beat. Prices are costs keys (scaled like every hire), set from the bot's measured purchase times: Level 8 (serve 16 premium customers) bought its old hires at 19/34/55 s of 178 s (longest phase 0.65); with this ladder at 19/34/54/86/119 s of 169 s (longest phase 0.20). skipGoals: goals whose cashier waits for the goal (shelves_full).

scrapHeaps._doc: Batch 3 (Doug): on every defend level (chance 1; outpost-ops#86), n scrap heaps (node.salvage_pile, a little scrap each, never regrowing) lie out in the wilds beyond the wall, at least outside units past the ring and within band of that, and roadGap clear of every attack road, so the player scavenges for the first defences.

medicPad._doc: R5 (Doug): on a defend level with guards and no med bay within the bots' farBay of a gate, a medic's hire pad stands outside the wall by an attack gate and off its road: wanted at [u, v] in the gate's frame (either side), kept at most near units from the gate's middle.

viewClear._doc: What the camera sees (it looks from the south, tilted): anything taller than a pad hides the ground just north of it. No pad's centre may lie in a building's footprint (its body plus the ground it hides), nor within wallShadow world units north of a wall (a ~1 m wall x cot 50). Walled attack levels are attacked only from attackSides, the sides facing the camera; a multi-side level takes as many of them as there are.
viewClear.realCamera_doc: ON rejects a layout when a pad (tower pads excepted) is hidden on screen under the real camera (yaw 45, tilt 30; src/viewVisibility.ts, the renderer's own test: 75% or more of the pad disc covered by a building, node, gate or wall). OFF (default): the same measurement is only reported on Built.padVisibility. Leave OFF until the shipped levels' pads have been moved, or most layouts fail.
viewClear.placeShade_doc: Doug, 2026-11-15: ON places with the real camera's shadows (src/viewVisibility.ts shadowTest, each model at its biggest size): a pad or a building's pad slot is never placed where a model already placed hides any of it, and nothing tall is placed where its shadow falls on a pad already placed (wall towers and walls are left out). Pads themselves touch their building on its south-east side (plot.json slots, tools/build-plots.ts).

defendSockets._doc: Batch 3 turret sockets inside the wall at each attack gate (none since Doug's playtest: the road pairs outside are enough): startInside per gate, at spots [u, v] in the gate's frame (u along the wall from the gate's middle, v outward, negative = inside; east and west gates use insideEW, the tower footprint being long along y). A site keeps edge from the (padded) map edge, wallClear from every wall, laneClear from every attack lane and siteR from every station centre; search is how far it may drift from the wanted spot. Gatherables on a socket's tower or pad give way, while more than keepForest ore scrap nodes are left.

defendRoad._doc: Batch 3 (after Kingshot): a defend level's map is padded by pad world units on every side, so each wave walks a long road from the map edge to its gate and the player can run out to meet it. The road out of each attack gate is lined with socket pairs: the first pair v = first units out, then every step (at most maxPairs pairs, endGap short of the edge); a tower borders the road: its footprint edge is a hand off the lane, towerU (towerUEW on an east or west road, the footprint being long along y) from the road line, to either side, and its pad stands directly behind it on the side away from the road (R14: the turret covers the road, the pad is out of the line of fire and in the camera view). The nearest pair stands from the start, pair k opens once k waves have started (the rest with the last wave). Every defence purchase (guard, tower, tower level) raises the next one's price by priceGrowth (the level's pads.defenceGrowth).

defendFree._doc: Wall-free defend levels only (outpost-ops#208; walled levels never read this). The main defence is a ring of tower sockets around the reactor: `sockets` sites at frac of the heat circle's radius at core level refLevel (level 2: the level-1 circle, 95, is smaller than the buildings round the core and holds only 2-3 sockets; a level-2 ring stays inside every later, bigger circle), never outside band (fractions of that radius), evenly spaced from phase degrees, each free to slide angleSearch degrees either way to find room; the nearest `start` stand from the start, the rest open one per wave; fewer than minSockets found rejects the layout. A socket's pad stands padDepth world units from its tower. The road pairs stay as the early forward post. lanesBeforeCore2: attack lanes at most this many. Early salvage floor (default off = 1): firstTowerScale cuts the first tower's price, earlyDrops multiplies the swarm of the first earlyWaves waves (more scrap dropped).

terrain._doc: Geography (R3 item 17). chance = share of levels per family that get terrain; pieces = [min, max]; sizes in world units; gaps are clearances to stations, the core, walls, the map edge and the straight lines residents walk.

search._loop: REDESIGN-R3 item 7: reject when the reference bot repeats one player trip (same source type, resource, target; trips a worker already performs are not counted) more than loopCap times in a row unless every leg of that trip has a takeover (a hire pad with that source and target costing at most takeoverMax; src/loops.ts, outpost-ops#87). Each reject raises an ease level by 1/loopEaseSteps: hire prices drop up to loopHireCut, core burn slows by up to loopBurnEase, level length shrinks by up to loopLengthCut, start currency grows by up to loopStartCurrency.

humanStars._doc: BACKLOG-R4 Batch 2: stars are earned by the human-view bot (bots HUMAN profile: human reaction, a little error, sees only the screen and the HUD), not the omniscient good bot. Each star objective (challenges and the time target) must be earned on at least minEarned of `seeds` in-level seeds, and at least one seed must take all three stars. 4 of 6 (two thirds) is a star a careful player earns on most attempts without luck or off-screen knowledge; one seed in three may miss it, which keeps the star a challenge. The good bot's old bar was 1 three-star seed in 10. levels:check replays the same seeds and fails a level whose human stars fall more than regressTolerance below the mean recorded at generation (rating.stars.human).
